newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PLOCK REFINERY UNIONS MULL JOINING PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PLOCK REFINERY UNIONS MULL JOINING PROTEST.

text.p: Union leaders at Poland's largest oil refinery, Petrochemia Plock SA, are considering joining workers at Poland's second largest refinery, Rafineria Gdanska SA, in demanding shares in their firms, PAP said on Friday.
On Wednesday workers at Rafineria Gdanska, in the northern port city of Gdansk, held a one-hour warning strike pressing for shares and a pay-raise.
PAP said late on Friday that union leaders at Plock were preparing referendum questions for workers on whether they would launch joint protests at both state-owned firms.
Unions active at Gdansk want workers to receive 15 percent of shares in the company for free, as envisaged by a privatisation bill passed last year.
They also demand a 17-percent pay rise in 1997 and a back pay increase for last year.

Rafineria Gdanska's spokeswoman has said management was ready to discuss pay issues with workers, but management has said the issue of free shares would have to wait until April 8, when a relevant privatisation law comes into force.
Plock and Gdansk respectively process about 10 million tonnes and three million tonnes of crude oil each year.
